summary: Iteration 5 validation of the 4 new FleetIntel features (server-side dashboard prefs, Incident PATCH, Fleet Health Score, Incidents index page). Backend: 35/35 pytest pass — appended TestUserPrefs, TestIncidentPatch (updates+404+audit), TestFleetHealth (shape+range+sort), TestIncidentsEnrichment on top of iteration_4 suite. Frontend: admin login OK, sidebar 'Incidents' link (nav-incidents) present and navigates to /incidents; incidents page renders all required testids (incidents-title, incidents-stats, filter-severity/kind/driver, search-input, export-csv-btn, edit-incident-*, driver-bd-*); severity filter shrinks list correctly; edit modal opens with all fields (kind, severity, driver, reported_cost, location, description, resolution_notes, mark as resolved) and PATCH succeeds with 'Incident updated' toast; Fleet page shows fleet-sort defaulting to 'health' and health-factors-<plate> pill visible on cards (e.g. '2 incident(s) in 90d'); dashboard exposes CONFIGURE TILES dialog and prefs round-trip through /api/users/me/prefs (GET+PUT verified via pytest).

integration_issues.issue: After saving edit (severity moderate->severe + Mark as resolved), the incidents list did not visibly reflect the change in the current viewport — filter dropdown appeared reset to 'Severe' and the row/stats bar showed 0 items despite the PATCH succeeding (toast 'Incident updated' shown, backend GET confirms severity=severe/resolved=true). Reloading the page renders the updated row correctly. Likely a stale-state issue in Incidents.jsx where the filter state or the incidents list is not re-synced after save.

action_items: MINOR: In /app/frontend/src/pages/Incidents.jsx, after a successful PATCH ensure (a) the incidents list is refetched (or optimistically updated) and (b) the filter-severity state is not inadvertently reset — verify the filter dropdown retains its user-selected value after edit save.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py continues to grow (~1916 lines) — still exceeds the 700-line guideline; splitting into routers (auth, fleet, incidents, analytics, prefs) is overdue.
IncidentUpdate correctly uses PATCH semantics with all-optional fields; audit action 'incident.updated' is emitted (confirmed by test_patch_incident_audit_log).
UserPrefs model is intentionally open-ended (dashboard_tiles only) — consider a schema-driven prefs namespace if more per-user preferences are added.
Fleet health scoring logic is server-side and returns sorted worst->best deterministically; scores are clamped [0,100] and status buckets are correctly emitted (verified).

GET /api/incidents enrichment (vehicle_name/vehicle_plate/driver_name) does N inline lookups — fine for current fleet size but consider a single $lookup/aggregation if the fleet scales past a few hundred incidents.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (appended TestUserPrefs, TestIncidentPatch, TestFleetHealth, TestIncidentsEnrichment — 35 tests total, all passing)

success_rate.frontend: ~95% — all UI elements/testids render and interact correctly; one minor stale-state after incident edit noted above

seed_data_creation: All test-created rows (TEST_* drivers, TEST_INCIDENT patch/enrich fixtures, TEST_M_driver_split) are auto-cleaned by their tests. One UI-created row 'UI_TEST_INCIDENT_<ts>' from iteration_4 was patched to severe+resolved during this run; if a clean list is needed, DELETE /api/incidents/{id} on Falcon-01 rows.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 4 iteration-5 features are functional. Backend suite is stable at 35/35. If main agent addresses the Incidents.jsx stale-state after PATCH, retest by: (1) navigate /incidents, (2) click edit-incident-* pencil, (3) change severity + tick Mark as resolved + Save, (4) confirm the row updates in-place (Resolved badge + new severity) without a manual reload, and (5) confirm filter-severity retains prior value.
rca_of_the_issue: For the frontend stale-state: Incidents.jsx likely mutates local incident state via optimistic replace but the filter-severity useState is being re-initialised or the incidents list is not being spliced after PATCH response. Compare with pattern in Fleet.jsx which does refetch on save.
